target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #95295

- **Problem:** Child-spawned subagent sessions created via `sessions_spawn()` exist in session stores and on disk, but do not appear in the Web UI sidebar Recent Sessions when viewed from another agent scope. Users cannot rediscover cross-agent subagent work from the sidebar.
- **Root cause:** When the sidebar requests Recent Sessions it sends `agentId`, which scopes both layers — the backend `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId })` loads only that agent's store, and the frontend `getVisibleSessionRows()` filters out `isSubagentSessionKey` / `spawnedBy` rows. Cross-agent child sessions are dropped before they reach the UI.

## What Problem This Solves

Multi-agent users can have persisted child-spawned sessions under agent scopes other than the currently selected chat agent. Those sessions exist in the gateway session stores and transcript files, but the default scoped sidebar request excludes the other agents' stores and the frontend projection hides child/spawned rows. The result is that completed or active subagent work cannot be rediscovered from the Web UI sidebar. This PR adds an explicit, default-off sidebar All-agents mode that preserves the existing scoped default while allowing users to intentionally load and render cross-agent child sessions.

## Solution

Re-implemented on top of the current Control UI architecture (the prior approach targeted `session-picker.ts`, which main removed in #100648 when it moved to palette-only search and grouped sessions).

- **Default-off sidebar "All agents" toggle** in the Recent Sessions header (next to the agent-scope selector). It is the only entry point; all other callers (CLI `sessions.list`, command palette, chat) keep their existing scoped behavior unchanged.
- When toggled on, the sidebar refresh sends **no `agentId`**. The backend already supports this: with no `agentId`, `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` runs `resolveAllAgentSessionStoreTargetsSync` (all agent stores) and `filterSessionEntries` keeps every entry including cross-agent children — so no backend/protocol change is needed.
- `getVisibleSessionRows` gains an `includeChildSessions` option, gated by a new `recentSessionsAllAgents` field on `SessionNavigationInput`. Default (off) preserves the existing scoped filter exactly.

## What changed

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` to `SessionNavigationInput` and `includeChildSessions` to `getVisibleSessionRows`; in All-agents mode, stop dropping `isSubagentSessionKey`/`spawnedBy` rows and skip the active-agent filter.
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — add `recentSessionsAllAgents` state, a `toggleRecentSessionsAgentScope` handler that refreshes without `agentId` (and restores the scoped `agentId` when toggled off), the toggle button in the ungrouped-session header, and the `recentSessionsAllAgents` input to `resolveSessionNavigation`.
- `ui/src/styles/layout.css` — styles for the `.sidebar-recent-sessions__scope` toggle button, matching the existing `.sidebar-agent-scope` pill.
- `ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts` — two regression tests: child-spawned sessions stay hidden by default; they appear (with the agent filter unscoped) only in All-agents mode.

## Evidence

Exercised the **actual gateway store-load root-cause path** (`loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway` from `src/config/sessions/combined-store-gateway.ts`, the exact function `sessions.list` calls) against a real multi-agent session store. Setup: copied the local `~/.openclaw` home to an isolated dir, which contains agent `main` (14 entries, including one real `sessions_spawn()` child `agent:main:subagent:737344ac-…`) and agent `microservice-log-query` (one injected cross-agent subagent child `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`, modeling a spawn from another agent scope). Both calls use the real repo code via `tsx`:

- **Sidebar All-agents path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, {})` (no agentId):** returns **15 store entries across 2 agents** (`main`: 14, `microservice-log-query`: 1), including **2 child/spawned rows**, one of them the cross-agent `agent:microservice-log-query:subagent:cross-agent-proof-child`.
- **Default scoped path — `loadCombinedSessionStoreForGateway(cfg, { agentId: "main" })`:** returns **14 entries from `main` only**; the cross-agent child is absent.
- **Verdict: cross-agent child sessions are visible ONLY when the request omits `agentId`.** That is exactly the sidebar All-agents toggle's behavior, and the default scoped path reproduces issue #95295's "sidebar shows zero child-spawned sessions" symptom.

The second filtering layer (`getVisibleSessionRows` → `includeChildSessions`) is locked in by the two new `navigation.test.ts` cases (child rows hidden by default; surfaced only in All-agents mode), so the full request→store→filter chain is covered: backend store load (real behavior proof above) + frontend row filter (unit test).

**Live Control UI browser proof:** after installing Node 24.18.0 and Playwright Chromium, started the PR worktree gateway on `http://127.0.0.1:19001/` against an isolated two-agent proof home (`main` + `microservice-log-query`). Playwright opened the Control UI, filled the Gateway Token, clicked **Connect**, waited for the authenticated sidebar, captured `proof-sidebar-scoped.png`, then clicked **All agents** and waited for the exact post-toggle `sessions.list` WebSocket response before asserting the DOM.

Post-toggle WebSocket request and response:

```text
TRACKING_POST_TOGGLE_SESSIONS_LIST id=64acb6cc-a213-490b-8401-dd9475ce9d29
WS_SENT_SESSIONS_LIST {
  "method":"sessions.list",
  "params":{
    "includeGlobal":true,
    "includeUnknown":true,
    "configuredAgentsOnly":true,
    "limit":50
  }
}
POST_TOGGLE_SESSIONS_LIST_RESPONSE id=64acb6cc-a213-490b-8401-dd9475ce9d29 ok=true
POST_TOGGLE_RESPONSE_RECEIVED true
```

Copied Playwright locator output after the successful response:

```text
LOCATOR text="cross-agent proof child" count=1
LOCATOR_FIRST_TEXT "cross-agent proof child" => "Subagent: cross-agent proof child"
LOCATOR text="microservice-log-query" count=1
LOCATOR_FIRST_TEXT "microservice-log-query" => "microservice-log-query"
LOCATOR text="subagent" count=2
LOCATOR_FIRST_TEXT "subagent" => "Subagent: cross-agent proof child"
```

Rendered sidebar text after toggling:

```text
会话
main
microservice-log-query
All agents
Subagent: cross-agent proof child
41h ago
Main Session
4d ago
Subagent: read_space_page
24d ago
所有会话
```

Screenshots captured from the same run:

- `proof-sidebar-scoped.png` — default scoped sidebar before toggling.
- `proof-sidebar-all-agents.png` — rendered All-agents sidebar showing `Subagent: cross-agent proof child`.

This directly demonstrates the changed behavior ClawSweeper requested: the browser sent the no-`agentId` All-agents request, received a successful response, and rendered the cross-agent spawned child row in the real Control UI sidebar.

**Automated proof gate:** the repository's `Real behavior proof` workflow parsed the authored `What Problem This Solves` and `Evidence` sections and completed successfully: [workflow run 29063489211 / job 86270110876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29063489211/job/86270110876) (`SUCCESS`, completed 2026-07-10T01:55:55Z).

## Verification

- `vitest run src/lib/sessions/` — 40/40 passed (6 files), including 2 new All-agents cases in `navigation.test.ts`.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` (covers `ui/**`) — 0 errors in changed files. (1 pre-existing, unrelated error in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`: missing `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` module, present on clean main.)
- `oxlint` on the three changed `.ts` files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk

- **Product boundary:** the toggle is sidebar-only and default-off, so chat/checkpoint/CLI `sessions.list` behavior is unchanged. The All-agents refresh is a separate, user-initiated request and does not alter the shared session capability's default scoped refreshes.
- **Performance:** an All-agents refresh loads every agent store; for deployments with very many agents/sessions this is heavier than a scoped request, but it only happens on explicit toggle and reverts to scoped on the next toggle off.
